findings: PROOF_CHAIN_SUBSTANTIATED: this deliverable ships an elaboratable SymbiYosys task, its PASS transcript, AND a negative control that makes the property discriminating. The proof is NARROW — one reset-safety property, not datapath correctness. See proof_scope.

CAMPAIGN_EVIDENCE_RECOVERED: the ORIGINAL v1.5.58 campaign's own formal artefacts — the very files the pre-correction `sby` / `sby_log` fields named — were located in this cell's own campaign directory and are NOW SHIPPED under phase2/stage1/formal/campaign_v1558/. See campaign_evidence. They carry no negative control of their own, and their results.json overstates coverage; both are disclosed there rather than repaired.

negative_control.mutation: one line deleted from the DUT — `p_reg <= 1'b0;` removed from the `if (rst)` branch of phase2/stage1/rtl/spm.v (line 98 as shipped). Nothing else changed; same harness, same .sby, same engine.
negative_control.result: the same task returns FAIL with the miter output asserted in frame 2 — the property therefore DISCRIMINATES and the 0.01 s PASS above is not vacuous.
negative_control.mutated_rtl_not_shipped_reason: a broken copy of a campaign RTL sitting in the evidence tree is a hazard; the mutation is a one-line deletion, reproducible from the description above.
negative_control.honest_caveat: the negative-control transcript ALSO contains `SMT Solver 'yices-smt2' not found in path.` and `ERROR: engine_0: Could not determine aigsmt status.` — that is the witness-RENDERING step failing for lack of yices, and it is NOT what produced the FAIL. The discrimination rests on the `abc pdr` line `Output 0 of miter ... was asserted in frame 2` plus `engine_0 (abc pdr) returned FAIL`, both of which precede and are independent of the missing solver. Stated explicitly so no reader mistakes a tool gap for the counterexample.

gate_rerun_on_this_deliverable.finding: NO_RESULTS: formal/results.json absent — nothing claims a proof (step 5 reports its capability gap upstream)
gate_rerun_on_this_deliverable.why: TWO reasons, neither of which is 'the proof did not run'. (1) The shipped artefacts were authored for the record by the F4 regeneration, not by `formal_property_run.py`, so no `formal/results.json` manifest accompanies them. (2) Even with one present, the gate's discovery is TOP-LEVEL-ONLY (`formal_dir.glob('*.sby')`, `formal_dir.glob('*.log')`), so evidence organised in a per-property subdirectory (`formal/reset_safety/`) is invisible to it — measured directly: with a results.json planted at formal/ the gate still reports `no .sby found under formal/`.
gate_rerun_on_this_deliverable.disclosed_because: a report that claims SUBSTANTIATED while the program it is named after prints FAIL, without saying so, is the same class of unverifiable certificate this correction exists to remove.

correction: vibe-ic#381 / review finding F10. #381 correctly removed a PASS resting on `phase2/stage1/formal/formal_spm_formal.sby`, a basename that existed in no published cell. What it could not know is that the stale pointer was discarding TWO real things at once. (1) This cell already shipped genuine, negative-controlled formal evidence under `formal/reset_safety/` (landed separately as 880d1a042) that no field pointed at. (2) The cited campaign artefacts were not lost at all — they are in this cell's own campaign directory, and they are now shipped under `formal/campaign_v1558/`, so the citation that started this finding resolves to real files for the first time. This report now cites only files that exist, quotes the tool's own lines from each, states exactly what is and is not proved, and discloses in `campaign_evidence.caveats_measured_not_repaired` that the recovered `results.json` counts TASKS as PROPERTIES and describes a functional BMC proof that was never run — shipped unaltered and flagged, not edited. The verdict is SUBSTANTIATED and deliberately NOT the program's `PASS`: `PASS` in this program's vocabulary means Step 5 as a whole passed, and one reset-safety property is not that. No number or citation was invented; every path cited above was verified present in this deliverable on 2026-07-26, and every quoted tool line was grep-verified in the shipped file that is said to contain it.

caveats_measured_not_repaired.results_json_shipped_unaltered: results.json is shipped exactly as the campaign wrote it. Editing an artefact so it reads better than the run it records is the defect this review exists to remove, so the overstatements below are disclosed instead of corrected.
caveats_measured_not_repaired.property_count_is_task_count: results.json says `"property_count": 2, "proved": 2`. That is TWO TASKS over ONE assertion, not two properties: `grep -c assert` on the shipped formal_spm.sv is 1. The `safety` task (mode prove, abc pdr, depth 20) and the `bmc` task (mode bmc, abc bmc3, depth 12) elaborate the same single assertion.
caveats_measured_not_repaired.no_functional_property_was_proved: results.json's bounded_vs_unbounded says 'functional property proved BOUNDED via BMC to depth 12', and formal_spm_report.md repeats it. There is NO functional or datapath property in the harness. The bmc task checks the same reset-safety assertion to depth 12. No arithmetic property of the multiplier was asserted and no equivalence miter was run.
caveats_measured_not_repaired.dead_macros: the .sby task scripts pass -DSPM_SAFETY_ONLY and -DSPM_RESET_AT_T0 respectively, but neither identifier occurs in formal_spm.sv or spm.v (grep -c = 0 in both). Confirmed at the elaborated source: both tasks' src/formal_spm.sv is sha256 818326ec98b44318d369bd3fdaaee22c8a352611ade205b70efe3013825e548a, one assertion each. The tasks differ only in mode and depth.
caveats_measured_not_repaired.no_negative_control: the campaign ran none, so these files alone cannot show the 0.01 s PASS is discriminating rather than vacuous. The regenerated evidence under phase2/stage1/formal/reset_safety/ ships one for the same property against the same RTL blob; it is not campaign output.
